title: Canary Rollforward and Surge Playbook Notes
body:
Notes from 2026-03-09 deployment ops call — working draft (capture of decisions, checks, and immediate actions for next 72h). Tone: operational, checklist-heavy. Pulls together runbook fragments for canary rollforward + surge/backfill behavior.

Attendees: Samira (owner), Liam (SRE), Hannah (serving-runtime), Diego (release eng), Priya (oncall coordinator), + shadowed by Eng rotation.

Goal: Agree on an explicit, minimal-risk rollforward path for canary failures observed in last nightly (higher tail latency on 16k seq workload). Define surge/backfill triggers and temporary capacity plans; pre-authorize emergency hotfix window and rollback criteria.

Summary of current state:
- Nightly canary (model: rdm-7b-16k) showed 95p latency spike at ~03:12 UTC on 03/08; p50/p90 stable. Error rate for streaming sessions increased from 0.2%->1.8% for 10 minute window.
- Correlation: increased queue depth on pool-gpu-us-west-2-b during GC/VM churn (relates to infra autoscaler adjustments).
- Canary auto-fallback executed but traffic cutover left ~120 in-flight sessions stuck; oncall manual drain required.
- No customer-facing incidents reported, but internal SLA jitter breached for Dedicated test tenants.

Decisions made (agreed on call):
1) Pause automatic canary rollforward for rdm-7b-16k until we validate the new batching/kv-cache patch in PR #2187. Manual gating required.
2) Implement short-term surge pool (2 x p4d-equivalent) reserved for canary backfill in us-west-2 for next 72h. Finance ok for temporary credit burn.
3) Add a check in the release conductor to detect >1% short-window error spike post-rollout and auto-hold subsequent batches.
4) Owner assignments for hotfix window (see action items).

Rollforward checklist (manual gating steps):
- Pre-deploy verification (Hannah): ensure PR#2187 landed to canary branch and passes the microbench harness (latency variance < 15% on 16k synthetic).
- Infra sanity (Liam): confirm autoscaler aims for target pool headroom >= 30% during canary time window; validate spot eviction forecast for next 6 hours.
- Canary metric snapshot (Priya): capture baseline p50/p90/p95/p99, error rate, queue depth, and KV cache hit rate. Upload to Confluence runbook section before cutover.
- Live observability probes (Diego): enable golden-traffic probe (small synthetic session with controlled token distribution) and scrubbing off any noisy customers.
- Rollforward dry-run: run with 10% traffic for 15 minutes, check canary stability metrics, then 30% for 10 minutes, then 100% if stable.

Surge/backfill strategy (temporary):
- Surge trigger: queue_depth_average > 70 and p95 latency > baseline+30% for >5m OR error_rate > 1% for >3m.
- Surge action: circuit in surge pool and route new canary sessions to surge pool; new host warmup includes KV cache preload using last-good prefix logs (Hannah).
- Backfill action: if surge cleared and p95 within baseline+10% for 10m, drain surge pool over 5m rolling drain to avoid thundering herd.

Hotfix window pre-authorization:
- Time window authorized: 2026-03-10 02:00-04:00 UTC (emergency only).
- Rollback criteria (pre-authorized): if after roll to canary-1 >1.5% error_rate sustained >10m OR if p99 > baseline+100% OR if manual oncall reports >5 stuck sessions.
- Escalation: immediate pager to release-emergency rotation, slack channel #release-hotfix, notify PM

Observability and dashboards to check (quick list):
- canary/rdm-7b-16k/latency (p50/p90/p95/p99)
- canary/rdm-7b-16k/error_rate and error_breakdown_by_type
- infra/pool-gpu-us-west-2-b/queue_depth and instance_evictions
- conductor/rollout/hold_reasons and last_hold_event
- golden-traffic/session-duration and token-emission-profile

Open questions / risks (notes to resolve):
- Are we confident KV cache preload will not introduce cache stampede on surge pool? (Hannah to run synthetic stampede sim).
- Spot eviction forecast model may be stale for us-west-2 — Liam to refresh with new pricing window data.
- Need confirmation from finance that short-term surge spend authorized beyond 72h if issues persist. (Samira to confirm by EOD 03/10).

Communication plan:
- Internal: update #release-ops with short summary at cutover, notify customer success if Dedicated test tenants flagged.
- External: hold until incident threshold met; if public-facing customer impact, prepare templated status blurb (see Confluence: public-status-templates).

Action items (owner - description - due):
action_items: Hannah Lee - Run microbench harness on PR#2187 and report variance; attach runs to Confluence - due 2026-03-09 20:00 UTC
Liam O'Connor - Provision surge pool in us-west-2 and validate autoscaler headroom; post infra snapshot - due 2026-03-09 23:00 UTC
Priya Nair - Capture canary baseline metrics and upload snapshot to runbook; coordinate golden-traffic timing - due 2026-03-10 01:00 UTC
Diego Ramirez - Add the conductor hold rule for >1% short-window error spike and add unit tests - due 2026-03-10 04:00 UTC
Samira Patel - Confirm finance authorization for 72h surge spend and escalate if needed - due 2026-03-10 12:00 UTC
Oncall (rotation) - Be ready to drain stuck sessions manually and escalate to release-emergency if rollback criteria hit - ongoing until 2026-03-12
postmortem-note: If rollback occurs, create a fast postmortem within 48h capturing timeline, root cause, remediation steps, and follow-ups. Link to REL-4821. Owner: Samira. Priority: P1 internal postmortem template.
